props.title: Centurion
props.initialSlug: Roman soldiers fight for survival behind enemy lines

sections.content: Centurion stands as a gritty, visceral take on Rome's mysterious Ninth Legion, blending historical speculation with brutal action sequences. Director Neil Marshall, fresh off his success with The Descent (2005), brings his horror-tinged sensibilities to ancient Britain, crafting a survival thriller that owes as much to First Blood (1982) as it does to classical epics. Michael Fassbender leads a desperate band of Roman soldiers through the hostile Highlands, pursued by Pict warriors in a chase film that emphasizes mud, blood, and the harsh realities of ancient warfare.

sections.content: The film sits within a fascinating mini-genre of "lost legion" movies that emerged in the 2000s, including The Last Legion (2007) and The Eagle (2011). These films tap into the enduring mystery of the Ninth Legion's disappearance from historical records around 120 AD. Marshall's approach differs by embracing a grimmer, more intimate scale, drawing inspiration from Celtic revenge films like Valhalla Rising (2009) and frontier survival narratives.

What sets Centurion apart is its unflinching depiction of ancient warfare's brutality. Unlike the polished battles of 300 (2006) or the nobility-focused conflicts of Gladiator (2000), Marshall presents combat as messy, desperate, and deeply personal. The film's chase sequences through Scotland's stark landscapes echo similar territory-based survival films like Apocalypto (2006) and The New World (2005), though with a distinctly British sensibility. sections.content: Centurion marked a shift in historical action films, moving away from the CGI-enhanced spectacle of films like Troy (2004) toward a more grounded approach. This influence can be seen in later works like Macbeth (2015) and The Northman (2022), which similarly embrace harsh landscapes and brutal combat while exploring ancient cultures. The film's focus on guerrilla warfare and survival rather than large-scale battles also influenced later historical thrillers like Black Death (2010) and Pilgrimage (2017).
